text:
Marina: quick dump of this morning's profiling run — 1) kernel selector seems to prefer cuBLAS path for Mixtral 8x32 at seq=512 even when aten-fused kernel is faster on our cards  
Jason: ugh that matches the spike i saw in the canary graphs, latency +18% on regen workloads  
Sara: did you capture the kernel timings? can you paste the flame output?
Marina: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# profile summary (seq=512, batch=8)
Mixtral-8x32: aten_fused_mm: 42ms | cublas_gemm: 58ms | kv_copy: 4.5ms | dispatch_overhead: 3.2ms
Llama-2-13B: aten_fused_mm: 37ms | cublas_gemm: 36ms | kv_copy: 5.0ms
Qwen-7B: aten_fused_mm: 29ms | cublas_gemm: 45ms | kv_copy: 6.1ms
```
Marina: selector picks cublas_gemm for Mixtral at this shape — probably due to our fallback heuristics using GEMM_estimate which is noisy at 8x32 dims
Ben: interesting — dims are heads=32, kv_dim=128? that mapping can flip the efficiency of aten_fused vs cublas. also Mixtral's rotary/fused-attn path is sensitive to RoPE scaling currently
Jason: the batching heuristics also contributed — we saw a lot of small, fragmented batches so the selector ended up favoring lower latency steady kernels rather than throughput-optimized fused ones
Sara: can you repro with continuous batching enabled (prefer_large_batches=true) and with kv cache hot path cold/warm?
Marina: repro steps in gist: https://redwood.internal/gists/abc123 (link) — with continuous batching on, selector changes to aten_fused and p99 drops ~11%
Alex: FYI we also observed a perf regression after the RoPE-scaling patch — sequences >1024 have scaled positional embeddings that cause extra memory copies in the KV path
perf-bot: deploy 2026-03-16T08:12 -> mixtral-opt branch rolled, perf alerts triggered: latency_sla_violation for /v1/generate on canary cluster
Ben: hypothesis: RoPE scaling changed layout so our KV copy code doesn't match alignment assumptions, causing suboptimal memcpy + extra cuda kernel for layout conversion
Jason: any quick mitigations? warm-up fan-out? draft pairing?
Marina: i tried draft-model pairing (speculative decoding) pairing Mixtral-8x32 primary + Llama-13B drafts — acceptance rate ~46% which is meh. But latency improved for accepted drafts. Rejection cost + extra model switch kills p99 when acceptance low
Sara: tokenizer mismatch created weird tokenization boundaries for Mixtral<>Llama pair in a few tests — acceptance fell. We need family-compatible tokenizer or a normalization layer in the speculative coordinator
Ben: acceptance tuning note: raise draft acceptance threshold to 0.87 for higher precision -> fewer accepted drafts but reduced wasted compute; tradeoff is tail latency for rejections
Alex: Another option: use draft of same family but smaller variant (Mixtral-lite) to avoid tokenizer issues and keep RoPE semantics compatible
Marina: we tried Mixtral-lite as draft -> acceptance 72%, p95 latency drop ~23%, cost delta -18%
Jason: solid. For immediate rollbacks, can we tweak kernel selector to prefer fused path for Mixtral dims when batch_size >= 4 and seq >= 256?
Ben: yes, we can add a heuristic rule: if model_family==mixtral AND heads>=32 AND kv_dim%64==0 AND batch>=4 -> prefer_aten_fused=true. Also add a calibration flag to run nightly microbenchmarks to keep the selector table fresh
Sara: need to ensure rule doesn't hurt Qwen or Llama variants. Add code to run quick verification on canary shard after selector change
Marina: i'll open a PR with the rule + unit tests. attaching perf diff snippet: 
```
- p99: 238ms
+ p99: 209ms
- throughput: 960 tok/s
+ throughput: 1024 tok/s
```
Marina: also adding kv-cache alignment fix — switch to 64-byte aligned buffers for RoPE scaled heads to avoid memcpy-kernel
perf-bot: benchmark job #453 finished: mixtral-kv-alignment -> perf improved on a100x2 but mixed on 3090 clusters
Alex: note: different GPUs have different kernel perf crossover points; selector should be device-aware (compute capability + sm_arch)
Jason: Agreed. Long-term: add per-card kernel curves in model catalog and let scheduler route requests by shape->device suitability. Short-term: apply rule + increase continuous batching threshold
Sara: i've seen weirdness with speculative coordinator where tokenizer mismatch leads to partial acceptance but wrong offsets. We should add a tokenizer hash check during draft pairing to reject incompatible pairings early
Ben: will add tokenizer-hash in the draft metadata and a fast check in the coordinator. Also instrument acceptance latency + compute wasted metric so we can tune threshold automatically
Marina: PR opened: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/2784 — contains selector rule, KV alignment, draft tokenizer-hash + perf tests. Request review from Jason/Sara/Ben
Jason: reviewing now. if CI passes let's canary to one region and keep perf alerted for 24h
Sara: adding integration test for Mixtral->Llama draft pairing to catch tokenizer boundary regressions
Ben: logging note: add an event when speculative draft is rejected due to tokenizer-hash mismatch so we can analyze frequency
Marina: thanks team. I'll follow up with canary graphs tomorrow morning and a short postmortem if the regression recurs
Alex: thanks — great thread. :thumbsup:
